paper.title: A minimax and asymptotically optimal algorithm for stochastic bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic K-armed bandit with one-dimensional exponential family arms (bounded means, bounded variance)
unmapped: Arm means restricted to a known bounded interval [mu^-, mu^+] inside the family's mean interval
Variance of the exponential family bounded by V (Pinsker-like inequality kl >= (mu-mu')^2/(2V))
settings.definition_quote: Each arm is assumed to be a probability distribution of some canonical one-dimensional exponential family $\nu_{\theta}$ indexed by $\theta\in\Theta$. ... we suppose that each arm $\nu_\theta$ satisfies $\mu=b'(\theta)\in [\mu-,\mu+]\subset I$ ... there exists $V>0$ such that $\sup_{\mu\in I} b''( {b'}^{-1}(\mu))\leq V<+\infty$.

symbols.V: upper bound on the variance in the exponential family

source.label: th:minimax_bound
source.quote: For any family $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying the assumptions detailed in Section~\ref{sec:settings}, and for any bandit model $\nu\in\mathcal{F}$, the expected regret of the kl-UC$\Bpp$ algorithm is upper-bounded as R_T\leq 76 \sqrt{ V K T}+(\mu^+-\mu^-)K.

results.notes: Regret is defined as sum of gaps times expected pull counts (pseudo-regret). The algorithm takes T as a parameter.

bound.regime: sqrt(22 V K / T) <= delta <= (mu_star - mu_a)/3

symbols.kl_delta: kl(mu_a + delta_p, mu_star - delta_p), the KL divergence between the shifted means
symbols.delta_p: free slack parameter delta (not a failure probability)

source.label: th:asymptotic_bound
source.quote: For any bandit model $\nu\in\mathcal{F}$, for any suboptimal arm $a$ and any $\delta$ such that $\sqrt{22 V K / T}\leq \delta\leq(\mustar-\mu_a)/3$, \E[N_a(T)]\leq \frac{\log(T)}{\kl(\mu_a+\delta,\mu^\star-\delta)}+O\left(\frac{\loglog(T)}{\delta^2}\right) which implies the asymptotic optimality

results.notes: This bounds the expected number of pulls of a suboptimal arm. The leading term has constant exactly 1, and only the second term is O(.). The proof gives an explicit bound: log T/kl + log((1/K)(1+log^2(T/K)))/kl + (16e^2+2)*2VK/delta^2 + 1.

symbols.KL_i: kl(mu_i, mu_star) in the exponential family

source.label: th:asymptotic_bound
source.quote: which implies the asymptotic optimality ... Choosing $\delta$ of order $1/\loglog(T)^{1/2}$ yields the asymptotic optimality.

results.notes: This is a corollary that the paper only claims informally: the limsup of R_T/log T equals the Lai-Robbins constant. It is not stated as a separate formal result.

cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic K-armed bandit, exponential family; uniformly efficient strategies; expected pulls of suboptimal arm
Minimax regret lower bound over the exponential family class F (adaptation of Theorem A.2)

cited_results.cited_title: Minimax policies for adversarial and stochastic bandits
